On VTES-L, Matthew Albritton wrote:
>
> A few questions for anyone so kind as to answer...
>
> Two Meths are left in the game. Me (Gangrel) and my prey/pred
(Tremere).
>
> Situation (1):
>
> The Tremere have grave-robbed Ricky Van Dempsy who earlier in the game
> committed diablerie. At a point later on, my prey has three ready
minions -
> one untapped tremere, one tapped tremere, and Ricky who is untapped.
I play
> Haven Uncovered on the untapped tremere, attack, and send him to
torpor. I
> then attempt to diablerize with another minion. My prey chooses to
attempt to
> block with Ricky. Can I now call a blood hunt against Ricky and burn
him? (I
> have voting dominance on the table w/edge) If so, am I still
continuing my
> diablerie attempt - at which point he must wake the other vamp to do
anything?

No.
The Blood Hunt must be called when the diablerie is committed, or not
at all.

> Situation (2):
>
> We're in combat. He's acting. He moves to long. I have to like it.
He plays
> Theft of Vitae. I play Wolf Claws and then Rotschreck. Alright
combat ends,
> he goes to torpor and all that but, do I still lose the blood from
Theft since
> it happens before damage resolution?

You cannot play Rotschreck. Your stike is not effective at long range,
so you are not "attempting to use aggravated damage against" your
opponent.

If you were at close range, then Rotschreck would end combat before
strike resolution (as you say), so you would not lose blood from the
Theft of Vitae strike.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
On VTES-L, Matthew Albritton wrote:
>

> "LSJ" <vte...@WIZARDS.COM> Wrote:
>
> > You cannot play Rotschreck. Your stike is not effective at long
range,
> > so you are not "attempting to use aggravated damage against" your
> > opponent.
> >
>

> What about the "whether successful or not clause"? I wasn't sucessful
because
> he moved to long...

No, his moving to long resulting in you *not* attempting to use
aggravated damage *against him* (but rather, against the air in
front of you). If someone had played a Direct Intervention to cancel
the Claws at close range, you would not be able to play Rotschreck
since you are not attempting to use aggravated damage against an
opposing vampire. It is not that your attempt is unsuccessful, it is
that there is no attempt.
